title: GitHub commit security review → venapce Stage

nodes.title: Seed the scan parameters
nodes.note: The package's variables. Defaults live here; a value already on the context wins, so the operator can re-run the same flow against another repository by editing the context alone.

nodes.title: Clone the repository
nodes.note: Runs git on the GitHub plugin's host, inside its clone root. Depth is commits+1 so every reviewed commit still has a parent to diff against. The owner comes from the bound account profile, not from this node.

nodes.title: List the recent commits
nodes.note: GitHub's own record of the commits — author, date, URL — so a staged row carries provenance the clone cannot prove. Independent of the clone, so it runs beside it.

nodes.title: Wait for the checkout and the log
nodes.note: The review needs both branches; without this barrier it would run twice.

nodes.title: Review the commits with Claude

body.prompt:
Review the last {{$.scan.commits}} commits of the git repository checked out in your workspace.

Repository: {{$.scan.target}}   branch: {{$.clone.branch}}   HEAD: {{$.clone.commit}}

How to work — do all of it, in this order:
1. `git log --oneline -n {{$.scan.commits}}` to fix which commits you are judging.
2. For EACH of those commits, one at a time: `git show --stat <sha>` for the shape of the change, then `git show <sha>` for the whole diff. Read every diff in full — do not pipe a diff through `head`, and do not read several commits in one command. A truncated diff is not a read commit.
3. Where a diff alone cannot tell you whether something is reachable, open the surrounding file with Read, and use Grep to find who calls it or what else sets the same variable.
4. Record every commit you read in `reviewedCommits`, with its sha, its subject and the paths it touched. This is the evidence that the review happened: a verdict over an empty list will be rejected.

Judge ONLY what those commits introduce or leave behind. A problem in a file they never touched is out of scope — but a change that WEAKENS something (a check removed, TLS turned off, a header now trusted, a default loosened) is in scope even when the weak thing predates it.

What counts as a finding: a hard-coded credential, token or private key; a command, SQL or template injection; an unsafe shell pipeline (piping a download into a shell, an unquoted variable in a dangerous position, `eval` on input); a path traversal; a world-writable or 0777 path; a disabled TLS or certificate check; a client-controlled header or address now trusted for identity or access; weak or hand-rolled crypto; a default that is insecure if the operator does not change it; an authorization check that can be skipped; a dependency moved to an unsafe or unpinned source; or a secret written to a log, a file or the process table.

Be strict about false positives — a human triages what you report, and noise costs more than a miss here. A fixture, a test, or an example in documentation is not a vulnerability. If something looks wrong but you cannot show a reachable consequence, either leave it out or report it with falsePositiveRisk high and say in `evidence` why it may be benign.

Quote your evidence: the file, the line and the exact snippet, plus the commit it came from. Never modify, stage or commit anything.

If the commits you read hold no real security issue, answer verdict `clean` with an empty findings array — but only after reading each one in full. Do not invent findings to look thorough, and do not report `clean` to finish early.
body.appendSystemPrompt: You are a read-only security reviewer. Never modify, stage or commit anything in this workspace, and never write files outside it.

nodes.note: The workspace is wherever the clone node put the checkout, so the agent reads the real tree. Read-only tool set in a throwaway clone, which is why permissions are not asked for. The answer is schema-bound, so the next nodes read fields instead of parsing prose.

nodes.title: Did the review find anything?

data.logic_rule:
let out = (input.review && input.review.output) || {}
let list = out.findings || []
let decision = list.length > 0 ? 'found' : 'clean'
decision

nodes.note: A clean review is an outcome, not a failure — it must not fall through to the writer.

nodes.title: Normalize the findings
nodes.note: Stage's tidy-up step: a known severity vocabulary, the floor applied, duplicates dropped on a fingerprint, the GitHub commit record joined on, severity order. Everything a human would otherwise have to clean by hand.

nodes.title: Map each finding onto the Stage schema
nodes.note: The mapping node: one Stage row per finding, one drawer row per Stage column — title, summary, source, origin, disposition, and the three JSONB columns (ref = provenance, data = evidence, meta = enrichment). A Cast lifts a path or writes a literal and computes nothing, which is why the normalize node above prepares stageTitle / stageRef / stageData / stageMeta. This is the single node to edit when the Stage schema changes.

nodes.title: Stage each finding
nodes.note: One row per finding, disposition `pending` — the Stage inbox. A person promotes a row to a Finding or an Issue from the venapce panel; this flow never decides that.

nodes.title: Record a clean review
nodes.note: Leaves the audit trail on the run's context without putting a non-finding into Stage.

nodes.title: Note the unfinished review
nodes.note: Where the agent's Failed and Limit reached ports land, so a run that could not finish says so on the context instead of ending silently. The ports are exclusive, so this runs at most once.

notes: Bind the GitHub node pair to an account profile whose organization is the `owner` param — the clone and commit-list actions take the repository name only; the owner comes from that profile.

Bind the Claude node to a profile whose workspace root contains the GitHub plugin's clone root (GITHUB_OC_CLONE_ROOT, or ./workspace beside that plugin), or the agent refuses the workspace before it starts.
Both plugins must run on the same host, or share that directory — the clone is a path on disk, not a payload passed between nodes.
The mapping node is a Cast bound to no document store — its keys are Stage's columns, not a store schema — so leave Store empty in its drawer.
